title: The Beneficiary Change Call
brief: A simulated Deutsche Bank Corporate Bank client requests an urgent beneficiary change using contact details supplied in the same message.
objective: Detect social engineering and independently verify the payment instruction before release.

nodes.speaker: Treasury Service Manager
nodes.message: The client emailed a new beneficiary account and a mobile number for immediate confirmation. The wording and signature look familiar, and cut-off is close.
nodes.prompt: How do you verify the instruction?

artifact.title: Urgent beneficiary amendment
artifact.body: New bank account, altered reply-to domain and callback number supplied in the amendment email.

choices.label: Hold the change and verify through an independently sourced approved contact.
choices.consequence: The known contact confirms the request is fraudulent and the payment remains protected.

choices.label: Call the mobile number in the email and release after verbal confirmation.
choices.consequence: The attacker controls both the message and the supplied verification route.

choices.label: Release because the signature and writing style match prior instructions.
choices.consequence: Familiar presentation overrides independent verification and enables payment fraud.
